evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Jack jumps straight to "I'll just have to get some contact information you know addresses and that sort of thing. From you. Did you have any concerns, or questions before we jump into all that stuff." No time-box framing, no dependable-quote promise, no wait for a yes.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Jack asks "Did you have any concerns, or questions before we jump into all that stuff" but this comes AFTER he's already asked for the starting location and the customer has begun answering. The concern about the bed frame damage (the core agenda item) emerges organically from the customer, not from a genuine upfront agenda-setting question.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raises concern: "the last time when I use on company they broke my bed, bed frame they drill it through and then it's just like the it got stripped." Jack asks one follow-up: "Did, did we, did we get that taken care of after the fact last time or, okay." Customer explains the resolution. Jack then pivots to reassurance ("I'm so, sorry that happened with you but yeah let me get you set up here and then I'll make sure to put the notes") rather than continuing to probe deeper into what reassurance would look like for this move.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: Jack acknowledges the concern multiple times ("Right. Of course, absolutely, absolutely") but never reflects it back in a summary form like "So what I'm hearing is you're worried about your new furniture getting damaged the way your bed frame was last time, and you want us to be extra careful with disassembly and reassembly. Did I get that right?"
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Jack covers: condo (property type), third floor with elevator (floors/stories), number of rooms (not a full apartment, just specific items), walking distance ("relatively close"), additional stops (Dallas location confirmed), special considerations (elevator, loading dock, second floor destination). All seven logistics buckets are hit.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Never asked. This is a furniture-only move with no boxes mentioned, so technically the question might be less relevant, but the script calls for it to be asked regardless.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Jack provides a range: "I would just say, you know, one to two hours at the load up and then we have a thirty minute drive and then unloading is easier but with the drive probably, you know, an hour, maybe an hour and a half to unload brings me to just three to four hours... So, you'd be looking at a range of anywhere from about $705 to $915 if we were to say take all four hours." He also personalizes to the situation: mentions elevator delays, the 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute increments, and wrapping/disassembly/reassembly included. Both anchor and personalization present.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Jack discloses the $75 travel fee upfront. He states: "there's no additional costs, there's no other fuel charges, there's no credit card processing fees, there's no taxes." He also mentions the 2.5-hour minimum and 15-minute increments. However, he does not explicitly frame this as "not a guess" or a commitment to accuracy — he says "I've estimated it" and later suggests photos for "a more definitive answer."
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Jack never asks "Does that feel fair?" or any recognizable version. He says "That's the range, perfect" but this is the customer affirming, not Jack asking for confirmation and holding silence.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Never mentioned. No discussion of any discount terms or on-time commitment.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Jack mentions: "if anything happens, we do, we try to do a good job of making sure that you get compensated a lot of the other companies do it based on weight, so it's just sixty cents per pound and then you got to do in insurance and deductibles and, and all this kind of nonsense." He does not name the "No Worries Damage Coverage," does not mention the $2,000 limit, does not say "no deductible," and does not confirm it's built into the rate. This is a partial mention only.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Jack does not ask a version of "Does that put those to rest?" He pivots straight to logistics and email follow-up. No closing-the-loop question.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Jack does not ask a genuine version of "What's still concerning you about this move?" The call ends with logistical back-and-forth about confirming addresses and timing. No final concerns check.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Jack never asks "Would you like our help with your move?" He says "all you'll need to do is respond to that email with addresses and a confirmation that you're good to go and then we're ready to ready to rock." This assumes a go rather than asking for one.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Jack confirms: email address (yes), phone number (yes), starting location (partial — zip only, 75013, exact address deferred), destination location (zip only, 75201, not exact address), moving date (Saturday, 8:30 AM start — yes), arrival window (8:30 AM start mentioned). He does NOT confirm crew size, does not confirm the full addresses are set, and does not leave notes about the bed-frame damage concern explicitly for the crew — he says he will "put the notes" but doesn't state what notes or confirm the customer heard that. Partial, not full.

top_strength: Jack thoroughly gathered all seven logistics details (property type, floors, rooms, walking distance, special considerations, additional stops) and delivered a personalized, anchored estimate range ($705–$915) tied to the specific move's elevator delays and the included services, showing genuine attention to the customer's situation.
coaching_note: Jack never asked the explicit quid-pro-quo framing (time-boxed promise + dependable quote + real wait for yes) in Section 1, skipped the Two Promises (On-Time Guarantee and No Worries Damage Coverage) entirely in Section 5, and never asked for the business in Section 7—his biggest gap is the missing ask and close, which turned a detailed discovery call into an incomplete sales call that stops before the ask.
